text:
Florida arrives on the second night of a back-to-back, having lost 4-3 at Washington last night, where Jack St. Ivany scored his first NHL goal. The Panthers are 3-2-0 in their last five and playing without Brad Marchand (knee), Anton Lundell and Sandis Vilmanis. With Marchand out, Lars Eller is up to 16:56 a night from 12:14. Boston has won three straight, most recently 6-2 at Pittsburgh, and is missing James Hagens (back). Elias Lindholm is next in line for his minutes.

The chances are close. At five on five, FLA has taken 53% of the expected goals (the quality of shots) and BOS 52%. Boston's results run ahead of that: finishing and goaltending are doing much of the lifting. Florida takes 5.2 penalties a game, which keeps feeding opposing power plays. The goalie matchup favors the home side. Projected starter Jeremy Swayman is +7.3 in goals saved above expected (how many goals he's stopped beyond what the shots should allow) this season and +26.5 last year, while Jacob Markstrom is at -0.6 and -16.0.

Among players to watch, Sam Reinhart has a six-game point streak and is 38% to score, while Matthew Tkachuk is 71% for a point. For Boston, David Pastrnak is 79% for a point. Our under-the-radar pick is JJ Peterka, 55% for a point, above what his season pace says (48%), with his ice time up to a projected 18:52 a night.
